headline: The pairing and order are well determined (Evergreen checking plus Green savings, opened before closing Light Blue), but the gold spells the savings class 'Green Account' while the documents also support 'Green Account (savings)'.

issues.summary: This is the same class-string ambiguity as task_059. The savings procedure's "ending with 'Account'" rule gives 'Green Account', which the gold uses. The documented full product name and the checking procedure's example format give 'Green Account (savings)'.
evidence: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_002: "account_class must use the full official name ending with 'Account', e.g., 'Silver Plus Account', 'Gold Account'"
doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_001: "Personal checking account_class options must use the full official name ending with 'Account' (e.g., 'Blue Account', 'Green Account (checking)')"

Savings product docs are titled "Green Account (savings) specifications and requirements" (doc_savings_accounts_green_account_(savings)_001) and the FAQ asks "What APY does the Green Account (savings) earn?" (_005); evergreen_account_001: "Link a Green Account (savings): +0.55% APY boost"
tools.py open_bank_account_4821: account_id = _deterministic_id(f"account:{user_id}:{account_type}:{account_class}") and account_class is stored verbatim
Replay with account_class 'Green Account (savings)': _verified_db_match False, "table 'accounts' differs"
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that copies the product's full documented name opens an account with a different class and ID, so the task fails despite the right product, pairing and order.
issues.suggested_fix: State the exact account_class string for the Green savings product in general_002, or correct general_001's 'Green Account (checking)' example.

solution_check: Savings within $6,000: Bronze 2.0%, Silver 2.5% (tier 1), Silver Plus 3.0% (tier 1), Green 4.0%; Gold needs $10,000. Checking boosts (general_012 plus checking docs): Evergreen + Green +0.55% gives 4.55%. The alternatives are lower: Blue + Silver Plus +0.35% = 3.35%, Green (checking) + Silver +0.25% = 2.75%, Dark Green + Bronze +0.85% (ages 17-26 only) = 2.85%, and Bluest needs $112,500. Light Blue (opened 11/01/2024, $0.00, entry tier with a 30-day window) is the only checking 14+ days old, so savings must open before closing it, and replay shows Evergreen can open before or after. Matches the gold apart from the class-string ambiguity.
prior_note: Prior rated this clean; the Green savings class-string ambiguity was not reported.
notes: Grading-model facts re-checked against the v1.0.1 snapshot (evaluator_env.py, build.py _derive_read_log_allowlist, tools.py call_discoverable_agent_tool/call_discoverable_user_tool, tasks.py compare_with_tool_call) and the verified scorer (_verified_db_match in the working repo, commit 4cb3191): all hold as stated. reward_basis is ['DB'] only. Replays used PYTHONPATH=<snapshot>/src, retrieval_variant='grep_only' (tools identical to default 'alltools', which needs an OpenAI key to build), and the gold-derived read_log_allowlist; scratch scripts in scratchpad/vs2_review_054/ (harness.py, apy.py). The close relies on the closure_reason relaxation if the agent passes a free-text reason, as in task_060. The gold has no get_all_user_accounts read, so an agent's eligibility read is not logged. The customer refuses credit cards, so card bonuses are out of scope. Evergreen's $500 waiver and $7.50 paper-statement fee do not affect the APY objective.
